title: Cardinality bound on the encoding-image over bad restrictions
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables whose width is at most $w$, let $d$ be a natural number, and let $\gamma$ be a fixed restriction. Write the Razborov encoding of $f$ with parameters $w, d$ on a restriction $\rho$ as a pair $(\gamma_\rho, \mathrm{aux}_\rho)$, where $\gamma_\rho$ is the extended restriction and $\mathrm{aux}_\rho$ is the auxiliary list. Consider those restrictions $\rho$ that are bad for the Boolean function computed by $f$ at depth $d$ — that is, the restriction of that function by $\rho$ has decision-tree depth strictly greater than $d$ — and that satisfy $\gamma_\rho = \gamma$. Then the number of distinct auxiliary lists $\mathrm{aux}_\rho$ arising from such $\rho$ is at most $(4w)^d$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
the width of f is at most w
d is a natural number and γ a fixed restriction
ρ ranges over restrictions bad for f's Boolean function at depth d
ρ's Razborov encoding has first component equal to γ
the image is taken under ρ ↦ second component (auxiliary list) of the Razborov encoding
replaced:
The number of distinct aux lists produced by the Razborov encoder on bad
restrictions with a fixed first component $\gamma$ is at most $(4w)^d$.
